claim: _run_cli sets stdout/stderr to PIPE whenever capture_output=True and silently overrides any stdout/stderr the caller passed; subprocess.run raises ValueError in that case. It also does not support `input=`, even though its docstring says it has the subprocess.run signature. Failure scenario: A future caller passing capture_output=True with stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, or input='...', gets separate pipes silently or a Popen TypeError instead of the documented subprocess.run behavior.

When a task uses a non-default registry_path, the suggested repair commands omit --registry-path. Following `models sync --apply` therefore modifies the default registry instead of repairing the registry that rejected the pin. The enable command has the same problem.

When the registry already has the starter's adapter and wire model under a different id (a 'covered' starter entry), the hint still says the starter entry is absent and tells the user to run `models sync --apply` to add it. plan_starter_sync never adds covered ids, so following the hint does nothing.

A starter spec that is already not routable (enabled=False) is returned unchanged, so under the default rule (or a locked adapter) it is written without the disabled_reason naming `puppetmaster models sync` and without disabled_authority 'models_sync'.

The CLI hard-codes the enable command string 'puppetmaster models set <id> enabled=true disabled_reason= disabled_authority=' instead of calling registry_sync.enable_command('<id>'). Failure scenario: The same command text now lives in two places, and the CLI hint goes out of date when enable_command changes.

_run_cli is documented as subprocess.run with different timeout handling (CHANGELOG: it has the signature of subprocess.run), but it passes kwargs to Popen, which rejects input=; input=... raises TypeError instead of feeding stdin.
On a rename line, _porcelain_path splits on the first ' -> ' even when it occurs inside a quoted source name, so it returns a fragment of the source name instead of the destination.

When a disabled starter model exists under a custom ID, this exact-ID lookup reports it as absent and recommends `models sync --apply`. However, plan_starter_sync recognizes the matching execution identity and deliberately skips it, so the recommended repair does nothing. For example, a disabled Haiku entry named `claude-code/my-haiku` reproduces this mismatch.

The registry-starter-sync doctor check counts absent starter entries on adapters the platform lock disables, so a deliberately locked setup warns forever. Failure scenario: A user locked to cursor only, with an old registry, always gets `warn: N starter model id(s) are absent`, including every claude-code/openai entry they can never route to. The only way to clear it is to append unusable disabled rows, and that changes the registry digest and fails queued pinned tasks.

A namespace-qualified pin such as 'codex/shared' is resolved (via resolve_model_pin, which keeps only the last path segment) to a different registry entry 'openai/shared' when only that one exists for the adapter, so the qualified identity is silently ignored and the task is bound to another model.

enable_command puts the model id into the shell command without quoting. A registry id that holds a space or a shell metacharacter (ids are not restricted) gives a command that, pasted into a shell, splits the id into several arguments, so `models set` fails or targets the wrong id. The disabled_reason text and unroutable_pin_hint tell users to run this command.

_run_models_sync catches only RuntimeError, but sync_starter_registry can raise OSError or PermissionError from read_text, the inter-process lock or write_private_text. Failure scenario: `puppetmaster models sync --apply` on a read-only ~/.puppetmaster/models.json, or one owned by another user, crashes with a Python traceback instead of `error: ...` and exit code 1.

On the BaseException path (and when the 10s communicate after a timeout fails), _run_cli kills the process tree but never waits on the Popen or closes its pipes, unlike subprocess.run, which uses `with Popen` and waits. Failure scenario: A KeyboardInterrupt or other exception during communicate() leaves a zombie child and open stdout/stderr pipe fds until GC. If a long-lived MCP server is interrupted repeatedly, or a detached grandchild keeps the pipe open past 10s, zombies and fds pile up and ResourceWarnings appear.

`models set <id> effort=<level>` for claude-code and codex replaces the whole `extra_args` list with only the effort flags, so other existing extra_args are silently lost. The code comment says unrelated payload defaults survive an effort change.

omp_pilot_check treats an existing but unparseable mcp.json as nothing installed. The 'mcp.json unreadable' detail is overwritten by 'no puppetmaster stdio entry in mcp.json'. With no omp CLI the check returns 'optional' (not installed) instead of the documented 'warn' for a partial install. pi_pilot_check overwrites the detail the same way.

The apply path reads and parses the registry file twice under the lock: load_registry in _plan_for_path, then json.loads(read_text) again. Failure scenario: The file I/O and JSON parse are duplicated on every apply. Loading the raw document once and building the specs from it would remove the second read and any chance of the two views drifting.

_agent_rules_check builds its display path with str(p).startswith(str(Path.home())) and then p.relative_to(Path.home()). A string-prefix match is not a path-ancestor match, so a rule file under a sibling like /home/bob2/proj when HOME is /home/bob passes the test and relative_to raises ValueError. run_doctor's guard then turns an existing, valid rule file into an 'error' row.

When the pin is given as an adapter model name and the registry holds that model under a different (custom) id that is disabled, the detail wrongly says the starter entry is absent and tells the user to run models sync, because the registry is looked up only by the starter entry's id.

The process-group fix covers only the five callers in codegraph.py; codegraph_repair still runs CodeGraph `status` through plain subprocess.run with a timeout, so the same timeout leak remains. Failure scenario: `codegraph status` hangs past timeout_seconds=30 (for example on a large or locked index). subprocess.run kills only the direct child, any Node children it started stay alive, and the 'no process left alive' guarantee in the changelog does not hold for repair runs.

A payload freshly produced by resolve_and_bind_explicit_pin for an agentic codex *-pro pin (hardened: model and pinned_adapter_model_name remapped to the base tier) is rejected by validate_pinned_dispatch, because it compares the remapped wire name with the registry's unremapped pin.adapter_model_name and raises 'executable model and pinned wire identity diverge'.

unroutable_pin_hint looks the starter entry up by id only, so when the registry already has the same adapter and model under a different id (the 'covered' case), the hint wrongly says the entry is absent and tells the user to run `models sync --apply`. Failure scenario: The registry has a disabled 'cursor/my-grok' with adapter_model_name 'grok-4.5'. A user pins 'cursor/grok-4-5'. The pin fails, and the error says to run `puppetmaster models sync --apply`. Sync reports 'skip cursor/grok-4-5: cursor/my-grok is the same adapter and model' and adds nothing, so the advice loops. The real fix is to enable cursor/my-grok.

_modernize_cli_args scans the whole argv, including the task text, for flag tokens. A task equal to '--format' (or '--max-nodes', '--max-files') is treated as a flag and dropped along with the next token. The CLI is then called as 'explore 15' (the task is lost) instead of with the task as the query.

A registry file that is not valid UTF-8 makes the check raise UnicodeDecodeError, because only RuntimeError is caught. Every other unreadable registry gives a 'registry unreadable' warning, and the check is meant to warn rather than fail on a bad registry.

ensure_codegraph_provisioned is documented as fully best-effort and never raising, but PUPPETMASTER_CODEGRAPH_PROVISION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=inf makes _provision_timeout_seconds raise OverflowError (int(float('inf'))), which is uncaught and propagates out.

The timeout test gives only 3 seconds for two Python interpreter startups plus the pid-file write before the timeout fires. Failure scenario: On a slow or loaded CI runner (Windows, coverage enabled), the grandchild has not written child.pid within 3s, and the test fails with 'the child did not start before the timeout' even though _run_cli is correct.

The apply write re-serializes the whole document with json.dumps (default ensure_ascii=True, fixed indent=2), which contradicts the docstring and docs saying existing rows stay as they are; it also skips validate_registry before writing. Failure scenario: A registry with notes like 'modèle rapide' or numbers like 1.50 is rewritten as 'mod\u00e8le rapide' and 1.5, and custom indentation is lost. The user sees a full-file diff after an 'append-only' sync, and nothing re-validates the merged list before it is published.

_porcelain_path strips the quotes of a git-quoted path but does not decode C-style escapes (octal UTF-8 bytes, escaped quote, backslash), so the returned path is not the real path; stat then fails and the file is counted as changed.
